headline.headline: KNICKS ROLL INTO NBA FINALS WITH 130-93 DEMOLITION OF CAVALIERS
headline.deck: New York completes sweep, reaches Finals for first time since 1999
headline.body:
NEW YORK — The wait is finally over. The New York Knicks punished the Cleveland Cavaliers 130-93 on Monday night to complete a stunning four-game sweep of the Eastern Conference Finals, booking a trip to the NBA Finals for the first time since 1999. The margin of victory — 37 points — left no doubt about which team ruled the East this spring.

Karl-Anthony Towns, who has been at the center of the Knicks' transformation into a genuine championship contender, was dominant throughout the series. The Cavaliers, who had leaned on Donovan Mitchell all season, found no answer in the conference finals as New York's depth and execution overwhelmed Cleveland on both ends of the floor. The 130-93 final was the punctuation mark on a sweep that felt complete long before the fourth quarter.

The Knicks now await the winner of the Western Conference Finals. For a franchise that last played for a championship when Patrick Ewing was still suiting up, this moment carries the weight of more than two decades of frustration. Cleveland, meanwhile, faces a summer of hard questions, though Mitchell has already reiterated his commitment to the organization and owner Dan Gilbert has vowed to rebuild around him.

secondary.headline: SVECHNIKOV'S OT WINNER PUTS HURRICANES IN COMMAND
secondary.deck: Carolina takes 2-1 series lead over Montreal after dramatic overtime victory
secondary.body:
MONTREAL — Andrei Svechnikov ended it at 14:06 of overtime, burying the winner to give the Carolina Hurricanes a 3-2 victory over the Montreal Canadiens on Monday and a 2-1 series lead in the Eastern Conference Finals. The Hurricanes, who finished the regular season at 53-22-7, have now won two straight after dropping Game 1 and look increasingly like the team best built to reach the Stanley Cup Finals.

The game was tied 2-2 through regulation, setting the stage for Svechnikov's heroics in the extra frame. Carolina now returns home for Game 4 with momentum firmly on its side. The Canadiens, who went 48-24-10 in the regular season, must regroup quickly — a loss in Game 4 would put them in a desperate spot against a Hurricanes squad that has shown the ability to win in multiple ways throughout the postseason.

secondary.headline: YANKEES STRIKE TWICE IN NINTH TO STUN ROYALS, 4-3
secondary.deck: New York rallies with two ninth-inning runs to escape Kansas City
secondary.body:
KANSAS CITY — The New York Yankees were running out of time and trailing by a run when they scratched out two runs in the ninth inning Monday to defeat the Kansas City Royals 4-3 at Kauffman Stadium. The comeback erased what had looked like a comfortable Kansas City cushion, as the Royals had answered a two-run Yankees second with a run in the sixth and another in the eighth to build a 3-2 lead entering the final frame.

The late rally completed a wild final three innings that swung the game completely. The Yankees had gone scoreless from the third inning through the eighth before erupting for the two decisive runs. The Royals, who had battled back twice to take the lead, absorbed a gut-punch loss in front of 26,162 at Kauffman Stadium. The game was played in 2 hours and 28 minutes.

secondary.headline: ORIOLES OUTLAST RAYS IN 13-INNING MARATHON, 9-7
secondary.deck: Baltimore scores four in the 13th to end a 4-hour, 12-minute battle
secondary.body:
BALTIMORE — It took 13 innings and four hours and 12 minutes, but the Baltimore Orioles finally put away the Tampa Bay Rays, 9-7, on Monday night at Camden Yards. The game was scoreless through five innings before both teams traded blows in extra frames, with the decisive blow coming in the bottom of the 13th when Baltimore plated four runs to secure the win in front of 22,388 fans.

The Rays drew within striking distance with two runs in the 11th and another in the 12th, but Baltimore answered each time before finally breaking through with the four-run 13th. Gunnar Henderson was hit by a pitch from Shane McClanahan during the marathon contest. The Orioles, who had also scored two in the seventh, showed enough resilience to outlast Tampa Bay in one of the longer games of the young season.

column.headline: TOWNS AND THE KNICKS HAVE EARNED EVERY BIT OF THIS MOMENT
column.body:
Twenty-seven years is a long time to wait. The Knicks faithful who packed arenas and sports bars Monday night to watch New York dismantle Cleveland by 37 points have earned every second of what comes next. This was not a fluky series win. It was a sweep. A statement. The Cavaliers, one of the better teams in the East all season, never found an answer. Karl-Anthony Towns proved every skeptic wrong about whether he could anchor a team built to win in May and June, not just November.

What makes this Knicks run feel genuinely different is the margin. Winning is one thing. Winning by 37 in a clincher, sweeping your way through the East, is something else entirely. Cleveland will lean on Donovan Mitchell next season and likely be formidable again. But right now, on the morning of May 26, 2026, this city belongs to the Knicks. The NBA Finals await, and for the first time in a long time, New York enters them as a team nobody sane would dismiss.

story.headline: NATIONALS ROLL PAST GUARDIANS 10-2, BOMB SIX HOME RUNS IN ROAD ROUT
story.deck: Washington erupts for six runs in first two innings, never looks back
story.body:
CLEVELAND — Washington hammered the Guardians 10-2 on Sunday, pouring on six runs in the first two innings and never letting Cleveland back into the contest. The Nationals sent a parade of hitters to the plate early, with Wood, Jr., Mead, Abrams, Young and Hoskins all going deep in a long-ball barrage that turned Progressive Field into a shooting gallery. It was the kind of performance that leaves a home crowd quiet by the third inning.

Wood's home run — his 14th of the season — headlined the offensive onslaught, while Abrams added his 12th as Washington piled up 10 runs on the strength of six extra-base hits. Jr. contributed both a double and a home run, his fourth, to pace the Nationals' attack. Cleveland could manage only two runs on the day, scratching across one in the second and one in the fourth before the Nationals tacked on two more in the sixth to salt it away for good.

Elsewhere Sunday, Baltimore survived a 13-inning marathon at home to edge Tampa Bay 9-7, with the Orioles pushing across four runs in the bottom of the 13th to end a game that saw 43 combined runners left on base. In Kansas City, the Yankees won 4-3 on a two-run ninth to take a 2-0 series lead over the Royals, while the Cubs fell 2-1 in Pittsburgh to extend their losing streak to nine games heading into Monday's rematch at PNC Park.

story.headline: KNICKS SWEEP CAVS, REACH NBA FINALS FOR FIRST TIME SINCE 1999
story.deck: New York dismantles Cleveland 130-93 to complete stunning four-game sweep of Eastern Conference finals.
story.body:
CLEVELAND — The suffering is over. The New York Knicks dismantled the Cleveland Cavaliers 130-93 on Monday night at Rocket Mortgage FieldHouse, completing a four-game sweep of the Eastern Conference finals and punching their first ticket to the NBA Finals in 27 years. Karl Anthony-Towns and the Knicks were never seriously threatened, turning what could have been a tense closeout game into a wire-to-wire demolition of a Cavaliers squad that had no answers all series.

The margin told the full story of a dominant night. The Knicks led throughout and stretched the advantage to a 37-point final, exposing Cleveland's inability to slow New York's offense at any point in the contest. Towns, who spoke with ESPN after the final buzzer, captured the mood in the locker room plainly. 'It's a good time to be peaking as a team,' the big man said. Knicks head coach Mike Brown noted afterward that his club took accountability all season, a discipline that showed in four consecutive commanding performances against a Cavaliers team that looked overmatched from tip-off.

For Cleveland, the questions begin immediately. Donovan Mitchell and James Harden both reiterated commitment to the franchise after the sweep, and owner Dan Gilbert vowed to 'dig in' and rebuild around the core. The Knicks, meanwhile, advance to face the Western Conference champion in the NBA Finals, a stage New York has not seen since Patrick Ewing led the 1999 squad. New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani wasted no time celebrating on social media, and ESPN's Stephen A. Smith, a lifelong Knicks devotee, declared on air that all the suffering had finally ended.

story.headline: SVECHNIKOV STRIKES IN OT AS HURRICANES SEIZE 2-1 SERIES EDGE OVER CANADIENS
story.deck: Carolina wins Game 3 thriller 3-2 on Svechnikov goal 14 minutes into overtime
story.body:
MONTREAL — Andrei Svechnikov ended it at 14:06 of overtime Monday night, burying the decisive goal to give the Carolina Hurricanes a 3-2 victory over the Montreal Canadiens in Game 3 of the Eastern Conference Final. Carolina now holds a commanding 2-1 series lead heading into Game 4 in Montreal.

The Hurricanes, who finished the regular season at 53-22-7 to rank among the elite teams in the Metropolitan Division, showed the resilience that has defined their playoff run. Montreal, a formidable 48-24-10 club out of the Atlantic Division, pushed Carolina the full distance before Svechnikov delivered the knockout blow deep into the extra session.

Game 4 is scheduled for Wednesday at Bell Centre, where the Canadiens will face the pressure of a must-win situation to even the series. Carolina has now won two consecutive games after splitting the first two contests, and Svechnikov's overtime heroics give the Hurricanes significant momentum as the series shifts back to Montreal.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINNING FAST AS NFL TEAMS RESHAPE ROSTERS FOR 2026
story.deck: Multiple franchises chase signal-callers while draft picks settle into new homes
story.body:
The NFL offseason has turned into a full-scale quarterback market, with several franchises scrambling to lock up their futures under center before training camps open in late July. The Las Vegas Raiders completed a blockbuster trade last week to acquire veteran quarterback Sam Darnold from the Minnesota Vikings, surrendering two second-round picks in the deal. The move signals a win-now approach from Raiders general manager Tom Telesco, who watched his team miss the playoffs for the fifth consecutive season in 2025.

Meanwhile, the New York Giants made the most significant move of their offseason by signing free agent wide receiver DeAndre Hopkins to a two-year deal worth $28 million, giving quarterback Daniel Jones a legitimate deep threat for the first time in years. The Cleveland Browns, still rebuilding after a turbulent 2025 campaign, used the fourth overall pick in last month's draft to select Texas quarterback Quinn Ewers, betting the franchise's future on the former Longhorn standout who threw for 38 touchdowns in his final college season.

Around the league, the defending Super Bowl LX champion Philadelphia Eagles remain largely intact after general manager Howie Roseman locked up cornerstone players through the offseason. Running back Saquon Barkley agreed to a restructured deal worth $45 million over three years, ensuring he stays in Philadelphia through 2028. Rookies across the league report to minicamp this week, giving coaches their first live look at the 2026 draft class before the grind of full training camp begins.
